column1: # ci/red-arms/batch14-spotcheck.tsv -- TEXTUAL spot-checks for #289 batch 14.
# Feed to:  bash ci/pump-red-arm.sh linux-clang-debug ci/red-arms/batch14-spotcheck.tsv
# The seam (ci/pump-seam-arm.sh, ci/red-arms/batch14-labels.txt) covers this batch
# broadly; these arms mutate the SOURCE instead, so the block as WRITTEN AT THAT SITE is
# what compiles and reports. The seam proves the primitive's forced path; only textual
# mutation proves the site's own miss block.
# ⚠️ THIS BATCH HAS ONE RECIPE SHAPE, SO THE ARMS PARTITION ON ENCLOSING CONTEXT, NOT ON
# RECIPE. Every site is `run_window_then_ready` + `drain_or_report` + `ADD_FAILURE` +
# `return;`. An earlier draft of this line explained that with *"no fixture in the batch's
# five files has a Clock"*, which is FALSE -- see the corrected paragraph in
# `ci/red-arms/batch14-labels.txt`, which carries the whole account rather than a second
# copy of it. The short form: two sites do have a real clock in scope and still take the
# unclocked drain, on a condition (no clock-parked frame can exist at that site) that was
# measured, not assumed. What differs between sites is where the `return;` lands and what
# the drain has to quiesce, and that is what these six rows sample:
#   row 1  TEST_F body, statement at TEST scope; the site's discarded-result comment
#          (`may fail due to null session_ handoff`) must survive the migration
#   row 2  TEST_F body, site inside a nested `{ }` block -- `return;` leaves the whole TEST,
#          not the block, which is what makes the recipe legal here
#   row 3  plain TEST body whose `.get()` was genuinely UNGUARDED before this batch, inside
#          a large shared-target binary (session_pure_tests) rather than its own executable
#   row 4  the site the CENSUS COULD NOT SEE (its `.get()` is seven lines below its window)
#          -- so this row is the only mechanical check that the extra 31st site is real
#   row 5  a future from `acceptor.async_accept(asio::use_future)`, NOT from `co_spawn`:
#          `ci/pump-get-sweep.sh` is structurally blind to this file (proven -- see below)
#   row 6  the second copy of a two-copy shape -- `test_live_identity_binding.cpp` holds
#          two `/open` sites spelled identically, in two tests, and this row arms the
#          one in the file's second test. (This descriptor named the FIRST test and
#          called it the second; the arm was corrected to match the descriptor's intent
#          rather than the descriptor softened to match the arm.)
# ⚠️ ROW 5 EXISTS BECAUSE AN INSTRUMENT WAS PROVEN BLIND, NOT BECAUSE THE SITE LOOKED ODD.
# `ci/pump-get-sweep.sh` recognises `auto NAME = asio::co_spawn(...)`. Re-derive rather than
# trusting this: copy the tree at HEAD, delete every
# `wait_for(0s), std::future_status::ready` line from a file, and re-run the sweep against
# it. Three of this batch's five files then report; `test_transport_factory_paths.cpp` still
# reports NOTHING, because its future never came from `co_spawn`. A silence from an
# instrument that cannot see the file is not evidence, so that site's guarded/unguarded
# status is hand-resolved and this row is its only mechanical arm.
# ⚠️ THE LIVE-TLS ARMS CAN SKIP THEMSELVES INTO A FALSE `SILENT`. Rows 4 and 5 sit in tests
# that `GTEST_SKIP()` when `FIXPP_TLS_FIXTURE_DIR` names no readable cert. A skipped test
# announces nothing, which this driver reports as "the miss branch did not announce itself"
# -- the same output as a real defect. Before believing a SILENT on either, check the arm's
# ctest output for `SKIPPED`.
# Columns: file <TAB> anchor <TAB> label <TAB> cmake-target [<TAB> ctest regex]
# The anchor must be unique in the file's CODE (comments are blanked before the search);
# the driver forces the FIRST `run_window_then_ready(` after it. Column 5 is omitted
# throughout because every target here registers a ctest of the same name.
